Chapter Ten: Wholeheartedness—The Practice of Living and Loving Fully
At the heart of rising strong, there’s something powerful—wholeheartedness. It’s all about living in a way that truly embraces vulnerability, courage, and connection.
You know, most of us don’t even realize how much we’re holding ourselves back. How often do we play it safe, protect ourselves from disappointment, or just stay quiet rather than risk being hurt?
Let me tell you about a couple who’d been drifting apart for years. One day, they decided to sit down and have a real, honest conversation about their fears and their hopes. It wasn’t easy—actually, it was pretty uncomfortable, maybe even painful. But it was also incredibly freeing. They discovered that wholeheartedness isn’t about being perfect. It’s about showing up fully, even when it’s tough.
Wholeheartedness really is a daily practice. It means choosing to be present, to speak honestly, and to be kind—not just to others, but to ourselves, too.
Imagine a manager whose team had just experienced a failed project. Instead of brushing it under the rug, she gathered everyone together and acknowledged the disappointment. She invited her team to share what they’d learned, to talk openly about what happened, and to support one another. What happened next? The team grew stronger and closer than ever.
So many of us believe that vulnerability is a weakness. But here’s something to pay attention to—vulnerability is actually where creativity, innovation, and real connection begin. When you choose to live and love with your whole heart, you open yourself up to the full richness of life.
I think of a friend who spent years hiding her struggles with anxiety. When she finally shared her story with a close group, she was terrified of being judged. But instead? She was met with support and understanding. By owning her story, she gave others the courage to share theirs, too.
Wholeheartedness isn’t about never falling down. It’s about learning to get back up every time, carrying forward the lessons you’ve learned, and just keeping on going. It’s choosing to embrace all the messiness of life—the beauty and the pain, the wins and the setbacks.
So, as you move forward, remember: living and loving fully starts with showing up, being real, and letting yourself be seen. That’s the heart of wholeheartedness.
